items.question_text: You are training a spam classifier. You notice that you are overfitting the training data. Which three actions can you take to resolve this problem? (Choose three.)
items.solution_text:
Overfitting occurs when a model learns noise rather than the underlying pattern, leading to high variance.
Getting more training examples (A) provides a more representative dataset, helping the model generalize better to unseen data.
Using a smaller set of features (C) reduces model complexity, preventing it from fitting spurious correlations in the training set.
Increasing regularization parameters (E) adds a penalty for large weights, constraining the model's capacity and reducing overfitting.

choices.text: Get more training examples
Reduce the number of training examples
Use a smaller set of features
Use a larger set of features
Increase the regularization parameters
Decrease the regularization parameters

items.question_text:
You are implementing security best practices on your data pipeline. Currently, you are manually executing jobs as the Project Owner. You want to automate these jobs by taking nightly batch files containing non-public information from Google Cloud Storage, processing them with a Spark Scala job on a Google Cloud
Dataproc cluster, and depositing the results into Google BigQuery.
How should you securely run this workload?
items.solution_text:
Option C adheres to the principle of least privilege by granting a service account only the specific permissions required: reading from Google Cloud Storage and writing to BigQuery.
Assigning the Project Owner role (Option B) violates security best practices by providing excessive, unnecessary administrative access.
Options A and D are incorrect because restricting access solely to the user prevents automation, and the Viewer role lacks the necessary write permissions for BigQuery.

choices.text: Restrict the Google Cloud Storage bucket so only you can see the files
Grant the Project Owner role to a service account, and run the job with it
Use a service account with the ability to read the batch files and to write to BigQuery
Use a user account with the Project Viewer role on the Cloud Dataproc cluster to read the batch files and write to BigQuery

items.question_text:
You are using Google BigQuery as your data warehouse. Your users report that the following simple query is running very slowly, no matter when they run the query:
SELECT country, state, city FROM [myproject:mydataset.mytable] GROUP BY country
You check the query plan for the query and see the following output in the Read section of Stage:1:

What is the most likely cause of the delay for this query?
items.solution_text:
The query plan image indicates a significant imbalance in the processing stages, which is a hallmark of data skew.
When most rows share the same key value (e.g., 'country'), BigQuery cannot evenly distribute the work across workers during the shuffle phase, causing some nodes to process disproportionately more data than others.
This uneven distribution forces the query to wait for the slowest worker to finish, resulting in the observed delay regardless of concurrency or partition count.

choices.text: Users are running too many concurrent queries in the system
The [myproject:mydataset.mytable] table has too many partitions
Either the state or the city columns in the [myproject:mydataset.mytable] table have too many NULL values
Most rows in the [myproject:mydataset.mytable] table have the same value in the country column, causing data skew

items.question_text: Your globally distributed auction application allows users to bid on items. Occasionally, users place identical bids at nearly identical times, and different application servers process those bids. Each bid event contains the item, amount, user, and timestamp. You want to collate those bid events into a single location in real time to determine which user bid first. What should you do?

choices.text: Create a file on a shared file and have the application servers write all bid events to that file. Process the file with Apache Hadoop to identify which user bid first.
Have each application server write the bid events to Cloud Pub/Sub as they occur. Push the events from Cloud Pub/Sub to a custom endpoint that writes the bid event information into Cloud SQL.

Set up a MySQL database for each application server to write bid events into. Periodically query each of those distributed MySQL databases and update a master MySQL database with bid event information.

Have each application server write the bid events to Google Cloud Pub/Sub as they occur. Use a pull subscription to pull the bid events using Google Cloud Dataflow. Give the bid for each item to the user in the bid event that is processed first.

items.question_text: Your organization has been collecting and analyzing data in Google BigQuery for 6 months. The majority of the data analyzed is placed in a time-partitioned table named events_partitioned. To reduce the cost of queries, your organization created a view called events, which queries only the last 14 days of data. The view is described in legacy SQL. Next month, existing applications will be connecting to BigQuery to read the events data via an ODBC connection. You need to ensure the applications can connect. Which two actions should you take? (Choose two.)
items.solution_text:
Option C is correct because the BigQuery ODBC driver leverages Standard SQL, and a view defined in Legacy SQL cannot be referenced by Standard SQL queries; thus, a new Standard SQL view over the underlying partitioned table is required.
Option D is correct because the Simba BigQuery ODBC driver supports authentication via Google Service Accounts, which provides a secure mechanism for applications to connect without involving individual user credentials.

choices.text: Create a new view over events using standard SQL
Create a new partitioned table using a standard SQL query
Create a new view over events_partitioned using standard SQL
Create a service account for the ODBC connection to use for authentication
Create a Google Cloud Identity and Access Management (Cloud IAM) role for the ODBC connection and shared "events"
